##### auto-generate-feature-pr
# Mirrors BaubleBar_Shopify_2026: on pushes to feature/*, bug/*, hotfix/*,
# open a PR into release/_candidate (if one doesn't already exist).

name: Feature PR

on:
  push:
    branches: [feature/*, bug/*, hotfix/*]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  stage_pr:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Extract branch name
        id: extract_branch
        run: echo "branch=${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: GitHub Pull Request Action
        uses: cea2aj/pull-request@84eb0c3478f13651e5649367941b867ca02d7926
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          destination_branch: "release/_candidate"
          pr_title: "Pulling ${{ steps.extract_branch.outputs.branch }} into release/_candidate"
##### auto-generate-release-pr
# Mirrors BaubleBar_Shopify_2026: on pushes to release/* (except release/_candidate),
# open PRs into dev and main.

name: Release PR

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "release/*"
      - "!release/_candidate"

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  create_prs:
    name: Create PR to ${{ matrix.destination }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        destination: [dev, main]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Extract branch name
        id: extract_branch
        run: echo "branch=${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Create PR to ${{ matrix.destination }}
        uses: cea2aj/pull-request@84eb0c3478f13651e5649367941b867ca02d7926
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          destination_branch: ${{ matrix.destination }}
          pr_title: "Release: Pulling ${{ steps.extract_branch.outputs.branch }} into ${{ matrix.destination }}"
##### ci
# Runs on every PR (feature/bug/hotfix → release/_candidate, release/* → dev and main).

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Lint, typecheck, test, build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test
      - run: npx vite build --mode injected

      - name: Bundle size
        run: |
          echo "### Bundle" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          ls -la build | awk '/bundle/ {printf "- %s: %.1f KB\n", $9, $5/1024}' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
##### nosto-preview
# Uploads release/_candidate to the Nosto preview on every merge (build + sources, so it can be
# pulled back with `npm run nosto:pull`). Customers don't see the preview. QA it with
# ?nostodebug=true → Debug Toolbar → Preview on.
# Going live is manual: Nosto Admin → Search → Templates → "Deploy latest and launch live".
#
# At release time, run it by hand on `main` so the preview holds exactly the release.
# Needs the GitHub Environment `nosto-live` (vars.NOSTO_MERCHANT, secrets.NOSTO_API_KEY, optional vars.NOSTO_GUARD)
# and the repo variable NOSTO_CI_ENABLED=true (on/off switch). See README.md → GitHub setup.

name: Nosto preview

on:
  push:
    branches: [release/_candidate]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: "Overwrite the preview even if it was changed outside GitHub"
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nosto-preview
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Push preview → Nosto
    if: vars.NOSTO_CI_ENABLED == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: nosto-live
    env:
      NOSTO_MERCHANT: ${{ vars.NOSTO_MERCHANT }}
      NOSTO_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NOSTO_API_KEY }}
      NOSTO_GUARD: ${{ vars.NOSTO_GUARD || 'strict' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test

      - name: Guard — preview changed outside GitHub?
        if: ${{ !inputs.force }}
        run: node scripts/nosto-sync.mjs guard

      - name: Build + push to Nosto (build and sources)
        run: npx nosto st push --push-sources --force

      - name: Preview state
        run: node scripts/nosto-sync.mjs info

# Mirrors BaubleBar_Shopify_2026: on pushes to release/* (except release/_candidate),
# open PRs into dev and main.

name: Release PR

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "release/*"
      - "!release/_candidate"

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  create_prs:
    name: Create PR to ${{ matrix.destination }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        destination: [dev, main]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Extract branch name
        id: extract_branch
        run: echo "branch=${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Create PR to ${{ matrix.destination }}
        uses: cea2aj/pull-request@84eb0c3478f13651e5649367941b867ca02d7926
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          destination_branch: ${{ matrix.destination }}
          pr_title: "Release: Pulling ${{ steps.extract_branch.outputs.branch }} into ${{ matrix.destination }}"
##### ci
# Runs on every PR (feature/bug/hotfix → release/_candidate, release/* → dev and main).

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Lint, typecheck, test, build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test
      - run: npx vite build --mode injected

      - name: Bundle size
        run: |
          echo "### Bundle" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          ls -la build | awk '/bundle/ {printf "- %s: %.1f KB\n", $9, $5/1024}' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
##### nosto-preview
# Uploads release/_candidate to the Nosto preview on every merge (build + sources, so it can be
# pulled back with `npm run nosto:pull`). Customers don't see the preview. QA it with
# ?nostodebug=true → Debug Toolbar → Preview on.
# Going live is manual: Nosto Admin → Search → Templates → "Deploy latest and launch live".
#
# At release time, run it by hand on `main` so the preview holds exactly the release.
# Needs the GitHub Environment `nosto-live` (vars.NOSTO_MERCHANT, secrets.NOSTO_API_KEY, optional vars.NOSTO_GUARD)
# and the repo variable NOSTO_CI_ENABLED=true (on/off switch). See README.md → GitHub setup.

name: Nosto preview

on:
  push:
    branches: [release/_candidate]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: "Overwrite the preview even if it was changed outside GitHub"
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nosto-preview
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Push preview → Nosto
    if: vars.NOSTO_CI_ENABLED == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: nosto-live
    env:
      NOSTO_MERCHANT: ${{ vars.NOSTO_MERCHANT }}
      NOSTO_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NOSTO_API_KEY }}
      NOSTO_GUARD: ${{ vars.NOSTO_GUARD || 'strict' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test

      - name: Guard — preview changed outside GitHub?
        if: ${{ !inputs.force }}
        run: node scripts/nosto-sync.mjs guard

      - name: Build + push to Nosto (build and sources)
        run: npx nosto st push --push-sources --force

      - name: Preview state
        run: node scripts/nosto-sync.mjs info

### 2026-09-16 — Mobile slider sections: suppress per-card image swiping, add card_image_mode to Featured Collection

**Context:** TAHARI-13008054312. On mobile, product card sliders (Featured Collection, YMAL, etc.) had two competing swipe targets: the outer product slider and the inner per-card image carousel. The inner one captured touch gestures, so swiping navigated a single product's images instead of advancing to the next product.

**Options considered:**
1. Liquid-only: skip rendering hover slides when inside a slider context. Rejected because desktop and mobile share the same DOM; desktop hover navigation needs the slides.
2. CSS `display: none` on individual slides. Rejected because the scroll container still captures touch events with nothing to scroll, and `querySelectorAll` still counts hidden slides.
3. CSS `display: none` on the entire `<hover-images>` element inside slider grids on mobile. Chosen: the primary image lives in a separate sibling element, so it still renders.

**Decision:** A single CSS rule in `assets/theme.css` (alongside existing hover-images touch styles) hides `<hover-images>` on mobile inside `.grid--mobile-slider` and `.grid--slider`. Placed in `theme.css` because it loads globally; section-scoped styles and `collections.css` only render on pages containing those sections, missing PDP (YMAL) and other surfaces.

Also added `card_image_mode` (Model/Product) setting to the Featured Collection section (`sections/section-collection.liquid`), mirroring the existing pattern from Products with Image.

**Context:** TAHARI-13008054312. On mobile, product card sliders (Featured Collection, YMAL, etc.) had two competing swipe targets: the outer product slider and the inner per-card image carousel. The inner one captured touch gestures, so swiping navigated a single product's images instead of advancing to the next product.

**Options considered:**
1. Liquid-only: skip rendering hover slides when inside a slider context. Rejected because desktop and mobile share the same DOM; desktop hover navigation needs the slides.
2. CSS `display: none` on individual slides. Rejected because the scroll container still captures touch events with nothing to scroll, and `querySelectorAll` still counts hidden slides.
3. CSS `display: none` on the entire `<hover-images>` element inside slider grids on mobile. Chosen: the primary image lives in a separate sibling element, so it still renders.

**Decision:** A single CSS rule in `assets/theme.css` (alongside existing hover-images touch styles) hides `<hover-images>` on mobile inside `.grid--mobile-slider` and `.grid--slider`. Placed in `theme.css` because it loads globally; section-scoped styles and `collections.css` only render on pages containing those sections, missing PDP (YMAL) and other surfaces.

Also added `card_image_mode` (Model/Product) setting to the Featured Collection section (`sections/section-collection.liquid`), mirroring the existing pattern from Products with Image.

- Decide where the Model | Product switcher (`collection-model-switcher`, `search.liquid:174`) lives.
- Never render theme custom elements (`quick-add-product`, `hover-images`, etc.) through Preact JSX; only as injected HTML.
- Search currently returns pages/articles too (no `type` param on the forms; `search.liquid:86-89`). Nosto is products-only. Mention to the client.

## Key risk: per-card requests and Cloudflare 429s

Dynamic cards fire one Section Rendering request per card (36 per page). The vault's rule (`plp-infinite-scroll-and-swatch-fetch.md`) is to never fire a request per product card, because Shopify's Cloudflare bot challenge returns 429s and isn't merchant-tunable. 4. PRD for 13175307071 per Ticket Authoring Prompt v2.
5. Vault: pattern doc and decisions entry once built and decided.

- Run the 429/perf gate before building the full UI? (asked, not yet answered)
- Is the third app embed `nosto-mc-embed-block` on `nosto/_candidate` intentional? (Bauble has only script + tagging.)

content.text:
**Untracked files:** these are in the Elie theme repo (`Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_2026`). I flagged them only so I wouldn't touch them. Doing theme work in a separate worktree leaves them alone.
- `package copy.json`
- `package-lock.json`
- `shopify-support-reply-to-alan.txt`
- `temp/delivery-promise-spacer.liquid`
- `temp/playwright.config.js`
- `temp/tests/pdp-gallery/`: README, helpers, and the a11y, desktop, mobile and zoom specs

In this Nosto repo, the only uncommitted changes are mine: the workflow changes and `docs/TAHARI-13175307071-context.md`.

**Does Bauble limit search to products?** No. Bauble's theme has the same stock Broadcast search as Elie's:
- Neither search form sends a `type` parameter.
- `sections/search.liquid:84-87` and `search-results-item.liquid:40` still handle pages and articles, both before and after their Nosto commit (`2d075dc`).

Their search is products-only because of how they turned Nosto on. When `rs_nosto_search_enabled` is on, `search.liquid` skips the whole Liquid results block, pages and articles included, and Nosto only returns products. So they didn't decide against content results; they just never kept them.

**If you want to keep pages and articles,** there are three options:
1. **Products only (Bauble's result).** Simplest. Queries like "shipping" or "returns" stop finding the help pages. That only matters if shoppers actually search for them, and Shopify's search analytics would tell you.
2. **Keep Shopify's page and article results in Liquid,** under the Nosto results. In Nosto mode, `search.liquid` can still loop over `search.results` and render only the non-product items through the existing `search-results-item`. That's a small amount of theme work and needs no Nosto setup. One catch: Shopify mixes those items into its own paging, so this works best as a short "Pages" block on page 1 rather than a full list.
3. **Nosto content search.** Nosto has some kind of content search, but I haven't checked whether it's available on Elie's plan or how it fits the starter. I'd need to look it up before recommending it.

Option 2 matches the SOW's "replicate the current experience" most closely for the least work. Option 1 is fine if you're happy to tell the client those help pages stop showing in search.

I've added this as an open question in the context doc.

# TAHARI-13175307071: Nosto search + autocomplete, working context

Handoff doc for any agent or session picking this up. Read in full before acting. Update it when a decision lands or a step completes.

Last updated: 2026-10-05

## Rules (from Patty, standing)

- **No code changes without Patty's approval of the plan.** As of the last update, the plan below is proposed and waiting for a go-ahead.
- **Commits:** never add `Co-Authored-By` lines. Commit or push only when asked.
- **Playwright / browser checks:** Shopify allows only one preview theme at a time per browser session. **Always** open URLs with the `preview_theme_id=<id>` param, then verify `window.Shopify.theme.id` equals that ID before trusting anything on the page.
  - `nosto/_candidate` theme: `https://www.elietahari.com/search?preview_theme_id=157709861001`
  - For verifying in-progress theme changes, Patty runs `shopify theme dev` on the theme repo and provides a dev preview theme ID. Use that one, with the same verification.
- **Theme branches:** branch from the latest `origin/nosto/_candidate`. Name: `nosto/feature/TAHARI-13175307071-<desc>` (the auto-PR workflow opens a PR into `nosto/_candidate`). Use a separate git worktree; the theme repo's main checkout has untracked files belonging to Patty.
- **PRD:** author with `/Users/pk/Documents/obs-roswell/Ticket Authoring Prompt v2.md`. There is no Monday PRD; the source is the SOW. Monday ID **13175307071**, project key `TAHARI`. Confirm each AC with Patty before finalizing.
- **Vault:** `~/WorkSpace/The_Intelligence_Layer/roswell-vaults/vaults/elie-tahari/`. Protocol: `/Users/pk/Documents/obs-roswell/Global/Documentation Protocol.md`. Only write verified facts; don't log undecided items in `02-decisions/decisions.md`.

## Scope

- SOW: `/Users/pk/Downloads/Elie Tahari — Nosto SOW - FINAL.md` (start 2026-09-30, go-live target 2026-11-11, $16k billed to Nosto). Vault copy: `06-financial/contract-nosto-sow.md`.
- **This round:** Nosto search results page and autocomplete only. Category pages, recommendations, OCP, consent gating and multi-market come later.
- **Design:** replicate the current live theme's layout and styling exactly. No new design.

## Repos and branches

| What | Path | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| Nosto templates (this repo) | `~/Documents/roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_Nosto` | working branch `feature/TAHARI-13175307071-search-template`; `main`/`dev`/`release/_candidate` all at `331b8ec` (pristine starter 1.14.0) |
| Bauble Nosto reference (snapshot of `BaubleBar_Nosto@3a1ab34`) | `~/Documents/roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_Nosto-bauble-reference` (worktree) | `reference/baublebar-nosto`, local only unless Patty pushed it. Reference only, never merge. |
| Elie Tahari theme | `~/Documents/roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_2026` | `nosto/_candidate` (branched from `develop/_candidate`, so it carries the unreleased PDP 2026 redesign; intentional per Patty) |
| Bauble theme | `~/Documents/roswell-studios/BaubleBar_Shopify_2026` | Nosto work is commit `2d075dc` on `origin/feature/BAUBAR-nosto-product-card` (PR #149), not on `release/_candidate` |
| Bauble Nosto original | `~/Documents/roswell-studios/BaubleBar_Nosto` | `release/_candidate`; docs in `docs/` |

## Done so far

- Starter copied and committed (`331b8ec`).
- GitHub workflows (uncommitted, on the working branch): Bauble's `ci.yml`, `nosto-preview.yml`, `auto-generate-feature-pr.yml` and `auto-generate-release-pr.yml` copied; the starter's `release.yml`, `deploy-pages.yml` and `copilot-setup-steps.yml` deleted. The only Bauble reference was a header comment, now pointing at the ET theme repo. `nosto-preview.yml` stays inert until the `NOSTO_CI_ENABLED=true` repo var and the `nosto-live` environment exist, and it needs `scripts/nosto-sync.mjs` (not yet ported).
- Vault (uncommitted, vault clone on branch `feature/pk-2`): `06-financial/contract-nosto-sow.md` updated to the FINAL SOW dates; Nosto rows added to `00-overview/timeline.md`, `04-engineering/repos.md` and `04-engineering/tech-context.md`.

## Approach (Bauble's "Approach A", adopted pending the 429 check)

- Nosto owns query, facets, sort, pagination, URL state and analytics. The Preact UI around the cards emits Broadcast class names so `theme.css` styles it.
- Product cards are theme Liquid via `<nosto-dynamic-card section="...">`, which fetches `/products/{handle}?section_id=<section>`. Each card type is its own `api-nosto-*` section:
  - `api-nosto-product-card`: renders `product-grid-item` for search results.
  - `api-nosto-product-card-mini`: autocomplete. **ET must render `search-product-item`** (today's dropdown card, `sections/predictive-search.liquid:187`). Bauble's mini renders the full grid card because their dropdown already did.
- Theme setting `rs_nosto_search_enabled` (default off) is the rollback switch. When on, `snippets/header-search-popdown.liquid` outputs `<div data-nosto-autocomplete>` instead of `<predictive-search>`, and `sections/search.liquid` outputs `<div data-nosto-search>`.
- Nosto selectors (`src/config.ts`): `dropdown: "[data-nosto-autocomplete]"`, `searchInput: 'input[name="q"]'`, `searchForm: "form"`, `results: "[data-nosto-search]"`. There are three header popdowns (desktop, mobile, mobile menu), so one autocomplete portal per popdown.

## Keep / adapt / drop from Bauble

- **Keep:** `scripts/nosto-sync.mjs`, `src/plugins/buildInfoPlugin.ts` (+ vite.config line), `nosto:*` npm scripts, `.nvmrc`, `.nosto.json.example`, the multi-popdown `injected.tsx`, `AutocompleteInjected` `closest(form)` binding, the dynamic-card rules in `theme-bridge.css`, test updates. Bauble also removed husky, commitlint and `AGENTS.md` (the starter's `AGENTS.md` says to commit with `--no-verify`).
- **Adapt:** `src/config.ts` values (36 per page matches `search.liquid`; `hide`-tag preFilter applies to ET); rebuild the `GridSkeleton` in `ThemeProductCard.tsx` from ET's `product-grid-item` (Bauble's uses classes ET lacks); `ThemeIcon` SVGs from ET's `icon-*` snippets; hardcoded English copy in `Serp`/`Toolbar`/`Pagination`/`NoResults`/`ThemeResults`; README, CLAUDE.md and docs with ET values.
- **Drop / replace:** Bauble's `docs/product-card/spec.md`. **Write our own** ET version from `product-grid-item.liquid` and `search-product-item.liquid`: image modes (model/ghost), sibling swatches, color count, single badge, cutline, price/sale, quick add, `hide` tag, plus a state list. Also drop all Bauble values: merchant `shopify-26757464148`, `baublebar.myshopify.com`, theme IDs `142783184980`/`145566990420`, `dev1-baublebar`, test handle `bubble-initial-necklace-gold`, `BAUBAR` prefix, "Amar" as approver, `baublebar-nosto` package name.
- **Version:** ET is on starter 1.14.0 and Bauble on 1.13.13. Keep 1.14.0's `VITE_NOSTO_ENV` support in `src/entries/dev.ts`.

## ET theme specifics to handle

- Don't reuse `api-product-grid-item`: its `aos_anchor: '||itemAnimationAnchor||'` makes the AOS observer throw (ET `sections/api-product-grid-item.liquid:6`).
- Section Rendering has empty `section.settings`. Pass `index: 99`, explicit `sizes` and `card_image_mode` (choose: hard-code `model`, global setting, or two sections).
- Keep `snippets/product-grid-scripts.liquid` and a `[data-products-grid]` wrapper outside the Nosto mount, so the iOS memory/scroll scripts (`card-scroller-window.js`) still bind. See vault `04-engineering/patterns/plp-infinite-scroll-and-swatch-fetch.md`.
- Don't render `collection-filters-form` in Nosto mode (its popstate handler fights Nosto URL state). Keep `product-info.js` and `grid-item.js` loaded.
- Decide where the Model | Product switcher (`collection-model-switcher`, `search.liquid:174`) lives.
- Never render theme custom elements (`quick-add-product`, `hover-images`, etc.) through Preact JSX; only as injected HTML.
- Search currently returns pages/articles too (no `type` param on the forms; `search.liquid:86-89`). Nosto is products-only. Mention to the client.
- ET constraints: never edit `assets/theme.js` (custom JS in `theme.dev.js`); tracking snippets go via `snippets/head.liquid`; don't hand-edit section content in `settings_data.json`; keep Consentmo, IPinfo, Klaviyo, Swap.

## Key risk: per-card requests and Cloudflare 429s

Dynamic cards fire one Section Rendering request per card (36 per page). The vault's rule (`plp-infinite-scroll-and-swatch-fetch.md`) is to never fire a request per product card, because Shopify's Cloudflare bot challenge returns 429s and isn't merchant-tunable. Run Bauble's gate before committing to the approach: first 8 cards ≤600 ms p75 on Fast 4G, CLS ≤0.05, no 429s paging 5 pages, plus a VPN test. Fallback is a native Preact card ("Approach B"). DVF (also Broadcast) uses Nosto native cards.

4. PRD for 13175307071 per Ticket Authoring Prompt v2.

- **Per-card pattern** (existing `api-product-grid-item` as a stand-in): 5 pages × 36 parallel requests, 1.5 s apart, 180 distinct handles → **all 200, zero `cf-mitigated`**. Page wall time 245–359 ms; p75 per card 203–226 ms; first 8 ≤288 ms. ~21 KB HTML per card (~770 KB per page). `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` (not edge-cached).
- **Batched pattern** (what `nosto-section-campaign` does: `/search?type=product&q=h1 OR h2 …&section_id=<section>`): 36 handles in one request → 200, **36/36 exact matches, no extras**, 682 ms (12 handles: 500 ms). URL ~1.7 KB for 36. Works as a lever if 429s show up; slower than parallel for first paint.

- **CWV risk that matters more than 429s:** today the cards ship in the initial HTML. With Nosto, LCP waits for the JS bundle → Nosto search API → card fetch → image (three sequential hops).

### Proposed optimizations (keep theme-rendered cards, no full Preact rebuild)

1. `lazy: true` (as Bauble does), so only cards near the viewport fetch.
2. **LCP image from Nosto data:** the skeleton renders the card's primary image (same URL/srcset/`sizes` as the theme card, `fetchpriority="high"` on the first row) as soon as the search response lands, so LCP doesn't wait for the card fetch. 4. Batched `/search?q=… OR …` section as a fallback if VPN/mobile tests show 429s (or a concurrency cap).
5. Measure with Lighthouse/WebPageTest on Patty's dev preview theme (mobile, throttled) vs the current Liquid search page on the same preview.

1. Keep `lazy: true`, so only cards near the screen are fetched.
2. Have the loading placeholder show the card's main image from Nosto's data, with `fetchpriority="high"` on the first row. That removes the wait on the card request for LCP. If the image URLs match exactly, the theme card reuses the cached image when it arrives.
3. Size the placeholder exactly like the card (1.5 aspect ratio) so the layout doesn't shift.
4. Keep batching ready in case 429s appear.
5. Once your dev preview theme is up, run mobile Lighthouse on it and compare against the current Liquid search page on the same preview.

Could you run the 429 test once over a VPN? I can't test that from here. I'll give you a script to paste into the browser console.

I've added all of this to the context doc. Next, if you approve: read the Nosto docs, upgrade `search-js` and `nosto-cli`, then start the theme branch.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

# Summary: Using Search Templates Starter

## Overview
Search Templates Starter is a Preact-based development environment for building custom Nosto search experiences. It's recommended for serious development work over legacy VSCode-based templates.

## Prerequisites
- TypeScript proficiency
- Git version control
- NPM-based tooling
- React or Preact knowledge
- Node.js 24+ required
- Optional: Agentic coding with LLMs (Claude, Copilot, Codex)

## Key Architecture Points

**Hosting & Deployment:**
- Templates hosted by Nosto infrastructure; no self-hosting required
- Artifacts uploaded via `nosto-cli`
- Injected through existing Nosto script tag
- No additional CDN or server configuration needed

**Configuration Requirements:**
- Search Templates enabled on account
- Correct CSS selectors in `src/config.ts` to target DOM elements
- Built and pushed templates via `nosto-cli`

## CLI Commands & Workflow

**Authentication:**
```
nosto login
```

**Development:**
```
nosto st dev
```
(Watch mode: automatically builds and pushes artifacts to preview)

```
npm run dev
```
(Local component iteration in isolation)

**Deployment:**
- CLI: `nosto st deploy` (implied from context)
- Or via Nosto Admin UI

## Preview vs. Production

Development workflow separates preview from live:
1. Changes pushed to **preview mode** first (not visible to visitors)
2. Access preview: append `?nostodebug=true` to store URL
3. Log into debug toolbar and toggle **Preview mode**
4. Deploy to production when satisfied

## Best Practices

- Maintain separate branches (e.g., `main` for production, `dev` for development)
- Keep repository ownership with active developer
- Use Git version control throughout

## Linked Sub-pages

1. [Getting Started](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/using-search-templates-starter/getting-started.md)
2. [LLM Examples](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/using-search-templates-starter/llm-examples.md)
3. [Repository Ownership](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/using-search-templates-starter/repository-ownership.md)
4. [Deploying](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/deployment-and-testing/deploying.md)
5. [Documentation Index (llms.txt)](https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/llms.txt)

# Deployment Summary

## Preview vs. Live Deployment

The Nosto CLI handles only preview deployments. Production requires manual promotion: navigate to **Nosto Admin UI > Search > Templates** and click **"Deploy latest and launch live"**. Deployments may take up to 15 minutes to become visible.

## Deployment Process

1. Test thoroughly in preview mode using the Nosto debug toolbar
2. Upload changes via CLI (automatically goes to preview)
3. Manually approve production deployment in Admin UI

## Rollback Procedure

To revert a problematic deployment:
1. Go to **Nosto Admin UI > Search > Templates**
2. Select the desired deployment, click **"..."** then **"Redeploy"**

The source code remains unaltered, allowing you to redeploy latest changes afterward.

## Disabling Templates

If no previous working version exists, disable search temporarily:
1. Navigate to **Nosto Admin UI > Search > Templates**
2. Click **"Disable Templates"** button

This provides a fallback when rollback isn't viable.

## Key Safeguards

**Preview First**: "All CLI uploads go to preview mode initially." Production changes require Admin UI approval. Previous versions are restorable via the Admin UI.

---

*Note: The documentation provided contains no information about CLI commands, multiple themes, Shopify-specific steps, caching delays, or versioning systems.*

# Search Templates Starter: Getting Started Summary

## Prerequisites
- Node.js v24+ from nodejs.org
- npm or yarn package manager
- Git version control
- Nosto account with Search and Categories enabled
- JavaScript/TypeScript familiarity

## Installation Steps

**Clone Repository:**
```sh
git clone https://github.com/nosto/search-templates-starter.git
cd search-templates-starter
```

**Install Dependencies:**
```sh
npm ci
```

## Configuration

**Environment Setup (Recommended):**
Create `.env` file with:
```
VITE_MERCHANT_ID=your-merchant-id
```

For Shopify stores, optionally add:
```
VITE_SHOPIFY_STORE_URL=https://your-store.myshopify.com
```

Alternative: `VITE_MERCHANT_ID=your-merchant-id npm run dev`

Find merchant ID in Nosto Admin UI under Account Settings, typically formatted as `platform-storeid`.

**Customize in `src/config.ts`:**
- CSS selectors for DOM element injection via React Portals
- Search behavior settings
- Component rendering options
- Custom queries for SERP, category pages, autocomplete

## Nosto CLI Authentication

```bash
nosto login
```
Then configure:
```bash
nosto setup -m your-merchant-id
```
Creates `.nosto.json` in project root.

## Development Modes

**Vite Dev Server (Local):**
```bash
npm run dev
```
Runs at `http://localhost:8000` with mock store, instant hot reload. Entry: `src/entries/injected.tsx`

**Watch Mode (Real Store):**
```bash
nosto st dev
```
Watches files, rebuilds on save, pushes to Nosto infrastructure. Preview with `?nostodebug=true` on actual store. ⚠️ Multiple developers overwrite each other's uploads—coordinate with team.

**Native Mode:**
```bash
npm run dev:native
```
Standard React/Preact app with single injection point. Entry: `src/entries/native.tsx`

## Development Tools

**Storybook:**
```sh
npm run storybook
```
No merchant ID required; uses mock data.

**Testing/Quality:**
- `npm run test` — Unit and integration tests
- `npm run test:watch` — Watch mode
- `npm run test:e2e` — Playwright end-to-end
- `npm run lint` — Check linting
- `npm run lint:fix` — Auto-fix issues
- `npm run typecheck` — TypeScript errors
- `npm run build` — Production build
- `npm run preview` — Preview build locally

## Key Caveats

- Without correct CSS selectors in `src/config.ts`, components won't appear
- `nosto st dev` requires merchant coordination to avoid conflicts
- Port 8000 auto-increments if in use; specify with `npm run dev -- --port 3000`
- Environment variable `VITE_MERCHANT_ID` essential for API connection

# Nosto CLI Summary

## Installation
- **Local (with npx)**: `npx nosto --help`
- **Global**: `npm install -g @nosto/nosto-cli`
- Included as dependency in Search Templates Starter projects

## Authentication Methods
1. **User Account**: `nosto login` (opens browser, credentials cached 8 hours)
2. **API Key**: Private Search API keys only (public keys unsupported)

## Configuration
**`.nosto.json` file**:
```json
{
  "merchant": "your-merchant-id"
}
```

**Required**: `merchant` (Nosto merchant ID)

**Optional**: 
- `apiUrl` (production, staging, or internal dev endpoints)
- `apiKey` (for authentication without login)

**Environment variables** (take precedence):
- `NOSTO_MERCHANT`
- `NOSTO_API_URL`
- `NOSTO_API_KEY`

## Commands
- `nosto setup -m YOUR_MERCHANT_ID` – Initialize config
- `nosto login` – Authenticate
- `nosto status` – Check template status
- `nosto st dev` – Watch files, auto-upload (excludes source code for speed)
- `nosto st push` – Build and upload sources + artifacts
- `nosto st pull` – Fetch remote state locally

## Production & CI
Production deployments not supported via CLI; use Admin UI instead.

## MCP/LLM Integration
**The documentation contains no mention of MCP (Model Context Protocol), an MCP server, AI/LLM integration, or an 'mcp' command.** The tool focuses on local development workflows with Git integration and standard build automation.

- **Global**: `npm install -g @nosto/nosto-cli`
- Included as dependency in Search Templates Starter projects

## Authentication Methods
1. **User Account**: `nosto login` (opens browser, credentials cached 8 hours)
2. **API Key**: Private Search API keys only (public keys unsupported)

## Configuration
**`.nosto.json` file**:
```json
{
  "merchant": "your-merchant-id"
}
```

**Required**: `merchant` (Nosto merchant ID)

**Optional**: 
- `apiUrl` (production, staging, or internal dev endpoints)
- `apiKey` (for authentication without login)

**Environment variables** (take precedence):
- `NOSTO_MERCHANT`
- `NOSTO_API_URL`
- `NOSTO_API_KEY`

## Commands
- `nosto setup -m YOUR_MERCHANT_ID` – Initialize config
- `nosto login` – Authenticate
- `nosto status` – Check template status
- `nosto st dev` – Watch files, auto-upload (excludes source code for speed)
- `nosto st push` – Build and upload sources + artifacts
- `nosto st pull` – Fetch remote state locally

## Production & CI
Production deployments not supported via CLI; use Admin UI instead.

## MCP/LLM Integration
**The documentation contains no mention of MCP (Model Context Protocol), an MCP server, AI/LLM integration, or an 'mcp' command.** The tool focuses on local development workflows with Git integration and standard build automation.

# Dynamic Product Cards Summary

## How They Work

Dynamic product cards fetch pre-rendered HTML directly from your Shopify store rather than building cards from individual data fields. The `nosto-dynamic-card` web component extracts a product's handle from its URL and uses it to construct a request to your Shopify store, retrieving the complete card template.

## Required Shopify Theme Setup

You must provide **either** a `section` or `template` prop alongside the `handle`:

- **`section` prop (recommended):** References a section ID from your product template. Shopify officially recommends this approach as "more robust."
- **`template` prop (deprecated):** An alternate template name. This usage is being phased out.

The component constructs the appropriate URL to fetch pre-rendered HTML when either prop is supplied.

## Starter Template Configuration

Two locations require setup:

1. **SERP**: `src/components/Product/DynamicCardProduct.tsx`
2. **Autocomplete**: `src/components/Autocomplete/DynamicCardProduct/DynamicCardProduct.tsx`

Example configuration shows changing the template name: `<DynamicCard handle={product.handle!} template="your-product-card-template" />`

Import the `DynamicCardProduct` component in `src/components/Products/Products.tsx` to enable dynamic rendering.

## Styling & Testing

"The styling for these cards is not included in the starter template's CSS." You must add your store's stylesheet to `index.html` for local development:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://your-store.com/store.css" />
```

## Notable Gaps

The documentation provided does not address lazy loading, placeholder behavior, performance recommendations, rate limiting, caching strategies, or click/add-to-cart tracking implementation.

Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__search_threads
entries.description:
Lists email threads from the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool can filter threads based on a query string and supports pagination. It returns a list of threads, including their IDs, `viewUrl`, and related messages (each with their own `viewUrl`). Each related message contains details like a snippet of the message body, the subject, the sender, the recipients etc. The `view` parameter controls which fields are populated in the related messages. By default (or with `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL`), it includes subject and snippet. Use `THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY` to exclude subject and snippet. Note that the full message bodies are not returned by this tool; use the 'get_thread' tool with a thread ID to fetch the full message body if needed. Threads with excluded criteria may still appear in the results. This occurs because Gmail identifies matching messages first. For example, if you search for -is:starred, Gmail will find an entire thread if it contains at least one unstarred message, even if other emails in that same conversation are starred.

Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

includeTrash.description: Optional. Include threads from TRASH in the results. Defaults to false.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of threads to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. Page token to retrieve a specific page of results in the list. Leave empty to fetch the first page. This is primarily used for pagination to continue fetching results from where the previous `SearchThreads` call left off, especially when the number of threads matching the query exceeds the `page_size` limit.

query.description: Optional. A query string to filter the threads. Natural language queries must be pre-converted into Gmail syntax queries to use this tool. If omitted, all threads (excluding spam and trash by default) are listed. Supported Operators by Category: Sender & Recipient: - `from:` — Sent from a specific person. - `to:` — Sent to a specific person. - `cc:` — Specific people in Cc. - `bcc:` — Specific people in Bcc. - `deliveredto:` — Delivered to a specific address. - `list:` — From a specific mailing list. Time & Date: - `after:YYYY/MM/DD` / `newer:YYYY/MM/DD` — Received after a date. - `before:YYYY/MM/DD` / `older:YYYY/MM/DD` — Received before a date. - `older_than:` — Older than a duration (for example, `1y`, `2d`). - `newer_than:` — Newer than a duration. Content: - `subject:` — Words in the subject line. - `has:` — Has specific content types (attachment, drive, youtube, document). - `filename:` — Attachment with a specific name or type. - `""` — Search for an exact word or phrase. (for example, `"holiday"`, `"holiday vacation"`). Note: Double quotes enforce strict contiguous phrase matching. For topic, discussion, or keyword queries, prefer unquoted keywords (e.g. `partner advertising` instead of `"partner advertising"`). - `+` — Match a word exactly. (for example, `+holiday`, `+unicorn`) - `rfc822msgid:` — Specific message ID header. - `AROUND ` — Find words near each other (for example, `holiday AROUND 10 vacation`). Labels & Categories: - `label:` — Under a specific label. The tool accepts label IDs, not display names. Use the `list_labels` tool to get the ID. - `category:` — In a category (primary, social, promotions, updates, forums, reservations, purchases). - `in:` — Search in specific labels (archive, snoozed, trash, sent, inbox). For example, `in:trash`, `in:inbox`. Archived and sent messages are included by default; use `-in:archive` and `-in:sent` to exclude them. Drafts are explicitly excluded by default by the tool. Use `in:inbox` to restrict search to the inbox only. - `has:userlabels` — Has any user labels. - `has:nouserlabels` — Does not have any user labels. - `has:*-star` — Specific star colors (if enabled, for example, `has:yellow-star`). - `in:draft` — Search in drafts. -in:draft means exclude drafts from the search results. - `in:sent` — Search in sent messages. - `in:anywhere` — Search in all folders (including spam and trash). Status: - `is:` — Search by status (important, starred, unread, read, muted). Size: - `size:` — Specific size in bytes. - `larger:` / `smaller:` — Larger or smaller than a size (for example, `10M` for 10 MB). Logic & Grouping: - `AND` — Match all criteria (default behavior). - `OR` or `{ }` — Match one or more criteria (for example, `from:amy OR from:david`, `{from:amy from:david}`). - `-` (minus) — Exclude criteria (for example, `-movie`). - `( )` — Group multiple search terms (for example, `subject:(dinner film)`). Examples: - `subject:OneMCP Update` - `from:user@example.com` - `to:user2@example.com AND newer_than:7d` - `project proposal has:attachment` - `is:unread -in:draft` To prevent overly strict queries, favor concise, keyword-based queries over long subject strings or full sentences. Avoid copying overly detailed subjects from the user prompt verbatim, as this often leads to search misses. Instead, extract the most unique keywords (e.g., subject:amazon \"delivery\" OR \"order\" instead of \"amazon order\"). Use boolean operators to broaden your search coverage. 84 CLAUDE.md
# CLAUDE.md — Elie Tahari TAHARI_2026 Shopify Theme

> **Read this before touching any file.**

Guidance for Claude Code when working in this repository.

> **Read the merchant vault first.** Everything non-code about this engagement — brand voice, audience, do-not-touch list, decisions, sprint/issue state — is canonical in the vault at `roswell-vaults/vaults/elie-tahari/`. This file is the **technical-only subset**. **The vault wins on any conflict.**

## Where vault context lives

Engineers usually symlink the vault as `../vault`. **Verify it before the first read**: run `readlink ../vault` and confirm the target contains `vaults/elie-tahari`. A symlink left over from another merchant resolves fine and has the expected subfolders, so it fails silently into the wrong client's vault. If it's missing or wrong, ask — don't fix it yourself or fall back to a direct path silently.

| Canon | Path |
|---|---|
| Merchant Context Document | `../vault/01-mcd/mcd.md` |
| Brand voice / Audience | `../vault/01-mcd/brand-voice.md`, `audience.md` |
| Do-not-touch list | `../vault/01-mcd/do-not-touch.md` |
| Decisions log | `../vault/02-decisions/decisions.md` |
| Active sprint | `../vault/03-pm/sprints/` (newest file — don't hardcode a name here) |
| Active issues | `../vault/03-pm/issues-index.md` |
| Repo registry | `../vault/04-engineering/repos.md` |
| Reusable technical patterns | `../vault/04-engineering/patterns/*.md` |

## What this is

Custom Shopify theme for **Elie Tahari New Jersey LLC**, built on **Broadcast v8.1.0**. Repo: `roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_2026`.

**Figma is the source of truth for every visual decision** — layout, spacing, typography, component behaviour, colour. Pull the relevant screens before writing code, and flag any Figma-vs-implementation conflict rather than silently picking one. File: https://www.figma.com/design/iBHKtwieSkMfWqYalNhK1v/Elie-Tahari---Amar-Copy

The one standing exception is **font size on the new PDP**, pinned in `px` to match Figma exactly rather than using the theme's relative units → `patterns/pdp-redesign-type-scale.md`.

## Commands and CI/CD

Shopify CLI `3.93.2`, Node `>=25.8.2`. Copy `shopify.theme.example.toml` → `shopify.theme.toml` (gitignored, never commit it). **Never point the default environment at the live theme.**

Branches: `feature|bug|hotfix/TAHARI-xxxxxxxx` (ticket ID required), `release/YYYYMMDD`. Feature branches auto-PR to `release/_candidate`; `release/*` auto-PRs to `dev` and `main`; pushing `release/_candidate` auto-deploys to the RC theme. Workflows in `.github/workflows/`. Conventional Commits.

## Architecture

Standard Shopify OS 2.0 layout. The pieces that matter when making changes:

- **`assets/theme.js` — never edit.** It's the Broadcast distribution build. All custom JS goes in **`assets/theme.dev.js`**, which is what `theme.liquid` actually loads. Keep it that way. (`assets/custom.js` is deliberately commented out.)
- **`assets/theme.css` is hand-editable** — despite its disclaimer there's no build pipeline in this repo. The risk is a future Broadcast version bump clobbering direct edits, same as any vendor file. `photoswipe.js`/`zoom.js`/`ajaxinate.js` look like dead code and aren't — don't delete them. → `patterns/vendor-file-editing.md`
- **`snippets/head.liquid`** — the most-edited file. All tracking (GTM `GTM-NZ499HTS`, Bing UET, Consent Mode V2, GSF pixels, Criteo, Clarity, Curalate, ShopMy, Adobe Fonts), font loading, and the CSS custom properties generated from theme settings. content.text:
Found the blocker: Search isn't enabled on Elie Tahari's Nosto account yet. The account (`shopify-35089973385`) has no search API URL in its settings, and our code can't fix that; Nosto has to switch it on.

**What I confirmed on your dev theme (`157823434889`):**
- **Theme side works.**
  - With the setting on, Broadcast's predictive search is gone. All 3 header autocomplete mounts are there, and the results mount sits inside the grid wrapper, inside `collection-component`, with the right settings.
  - Both card sections render for 3 products: no Liquid errors, no leftover placeholders. The grid card has quick add and lazy images; the dropdown card has no quick add.
- **Our UI loads on your page.** I injected the local production build in Playwright, which uploads nothing to Nosto. The toolbar shows "Sort / Relevance" and the Model | Product switcher, and the loading placeholders appear.

content.text:
No. `?nostodebug=true` works on its own on any page; it's Nosto's parameter and has nothing to do with Shopify's theme preview. The two are separate "previews":

| Parameter | Whose | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `preview_theme_id=<id>` | Shopify | Shows a theme that isn't published, like your dev theme |
| `nostodebug=true` | Nosto | Opens Nosto's debug toolbar. After you log in there, a **Preview** toggle shows Nosto templates that are uploaded but not live yet |

Which you need depends on what you're testing:
- **Just checking whether the toolbar shows Search:** `https://www.elietahari.com/?nostodebug=true` is enough. This works on the live theme, because the Nosto embeds are enabled there too.
- **Testing our work later:** you'll need both: `?preview_theme_id=157823434889&nostodebug=true` loads your dev theme with the setting on, and the toolbar's Preview toggle loads our uploaded templates.

One thing I haven't verified: whether the toolbar stays open after the first page (via a cookie or session) or needs `nostodebug=true` on every page. If it disappears as you click around, add the parameter again.

1. Open `https://www.elietahari.com/?preview_theme_id=157823434889`.
2. Then open `https://www.elietahari.com/search?q=dress&nostodebug=true`. The preview cookie keeps you on the dev theme.
3. Check you're on the right theme with `Shopify.theme.id` in the console, as with Playwright.

They come from the starter's `.github/dependabot.yml`, which arrived with the initial copy. It's on `main`, and GitHub runs Dependabot from the default branch, so once `main` was pushed it opened its weekly npm update PRs, up to 10 at a time. There are currently **8 open Dependabot PRs**, each with its own branch.

Bauble deleted this file on purpose (`b4d6382`, "ci: trim .github to the workflows we use"). When I copied their workflows I removed the starter's other workflows but left `dependabot.yml` and the PR template in place, and flagged them as open. It should have been on the list to remove.

content.text:
Dependabot keeps dependencies up to date automatically. Every week it checks npm for newer versions of the packages in `package.json` and opens a PR for each update or group of updates. The PR runs CI, so you can see whether it still builds and passes tests, then merge.

The starter has it because Nosto maintains the starter as a living project, and they want it to track the latest `search-js`, Vite, Storybook and so on.

For our repo it's mostly noise:
- **Most of the packages are dev tools:** Storybook, ESLint, Vitest, Stylelint and similar. Updating them doesn't change anything shoppers see.
- **Some of the configured groups aren't in our repo anymore.** It still lists commitlint and semantic-release groups, but we removed both.
- **Each merged update changes the template build**, and with our branch flow (feature → `release/_candidate` → Nosto preview) every one would need its own QA pass to stay safe.
- **Nothing reviews them.** At 10 PRs a week, unreviewed Dependabot PRs pile up, which is what you're seeing.

What actually matters (`@nosto/search-js`, `@nosto/web-components`, `@nosto/nosto-cli`) is better updated on purpose, when a Nosto release brings something we need. That's what we did yesterday with `search-js` and `nosto-cli`.

The one part worth keeping is **security alerts.** That's a separate repo setting, not this file. GitHub can still tell you when a package has a known vulnerability, without the weekly PR stream.

So I'd remove the file and close the 8 PRs, as Bauble did, and leave security alerts on in the repo settings.

# BaubleBar_Nosto: instructions for Claude Code

Nosto search front end for the BaubleBar Shopify store (Preact, TypeScript, Vite), built on `Nosto/search-templates-starter@1.13.13`. **Read [`README.md`](README.md) first**: features, how it works, project structure, theme integration, release process.

The theme is the sibling repo `../BaubleBar_Shopify_2026` (Broadcast). It renders the product cards and quick view; changes there follow its own `CLAUDE.md`.

## Architecture rules
- **The theme renders product cards.** Use `ProductCard` (`<nosto-dynamic-card>` + a theme section). Never rebuild the card or quick view in Preact; the starter's Preact card in `.unused/preact-card/` is a fallback only if theme cards become too slow, and needs Amar's approval.
- **Never render theme custom elements through JSX** (`grid-item`, `quick-add-product`, `hover-images`, `rs-product-item-swatches`, `popout-select`, `range-slider`, `collapsible-elements`, …). They read their children in the constructor, so they need parsed HTML. Either inject theme HTML (like `DynamicCard`) or reuse the theme's markup and classes and implement the behaviour in Preact (like `SortPopout`, `FilterGroup`, `ThemeRange`).
- **Use the theme's markup and CSS classes.** Nosto-only styles go in `src/styles.css` with an `ns-` prefix. No CSS Modules, no other stylesheets.
- **Theme options come from `src/lib/themeSettings.ts` only.** It owns the mount selectors and reads the "RS: Nosto Settings" `data-*` attributes, always with a fallback. Grid columns are theme CSS variables, not Nosto code.
- **Request only the product fields the code reads** (`productFields` in `src/config.ts`). Add a field there before reading it; setting `fields` replaces Nosto's defaults.
- **Don't load theme JS that rewrites the grid** on pages Nosto renders (`collection-filters-form.js`, `ajaxinate.js`).
- **Theme sections fetched by Nosto** (`api-nosto-*`): don't reuse `api-product-grid-item` (its `||itemAnimationAnchor||` placeholder breaks the AOS observer); pass `sizes` and `index` explicitly (`section.settings` is empty in Section Rendering).

## Code structure
- One feature → `src/features/<feature>/`; two or more → `src/shared/`; theme building block → `src/elements/`; no UI → `src/lib/`. Tests mirror `src/` under `test/`.
- `.unused/` is reference only (not built, linted or tested). Don't import from it; `git mv` code back into `src/` if it's needed.
- Prettier: 120 columns, no semicolons, double quotes. Run it on the files you changed only (`npx prettier --write <files>`), never on whole folders.

## Before calling a task done
- Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test` (and `npm run test:e2e` if you touched search flow, URL state or mount markup). **Judge each by its exit code**, not by grepping the output: an ESLint crash prints no "error" line.
- For UI changes, check the real store with the production bundle (see the `nosto-theme-integration` skill → "Verify on the live store"). Unit tests and `dev:mocked` can't render theme cards.
- **If `package-lock.json` changed:** npm on macOS drops top-level optional entries (`@emnapi/core`, `@emnapi/runtime`, `@emnapi/wasi-threads`, `jiti`) that Linux CI needs, and `npm ci` then fails only in CI. Diff against `release/_candidate` and restore them.

## Git and releases
- Never `git commit --no-verify`. Commits follow Conventional Commits (`feat(serp): …`, `fix: …`).
- Branches: `feature/BAUBAR-*` from `dev` → PR into `release/_candidate` → `release/BAUBAR-vYYYY.WW` → `dev` + `main`. Never force-push `main`, `dev` or `release/_candidate`.
- Never commit `.env`, `.nosto.json` or `.nostocache`.
- **Never put anything live.** Going live is manual in Nosto Admin, done by Amar. Don't run `nosto dp deploy`. `npm run nosto:dev` is fine, but the preview is shared with CI, so say when you use it.
- The published Shopify theme must contain the `api-nosto-*` sections and mounts **before** a Nosto release goes live.

## Skills (`.claude/skills/`)

| When | Skill |
|---|---|
| Adding a card type, theme setting, feature or mount; verifying on the store; changing dependencies | `nosto-theme-integration` |
| Editing `**/*.tsx` | `search-templates-preact` |
| Editing `test/**/*` | `search-templates-testing` |
| Editing any `*.ts` / `*.tsx` | `search-templates-typescript` (alongside the above) |

.claude/skills/search-templates-testing/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/search-templates-typescript/SKILL.md

content.text:
That's the authoritative contract. Here's what BaubleBar's settings are, read from the Nosto side (`src/lib/themeSettings.ts`):

**On the results mount** (`[data-nosto-search]` for search, `[data-nosto-collection]` for category):
| Attribute | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `data-pagination` | `numbers` / `load-more` / `infinite` | `numbers` |
| `data-page-size` | 1–100 (collection page; search uses the default) | 36 |

**On each autocomplete mount** (`[data-nosto-autocomplete]`):
| Attribute | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `data-suggestions` | boolean | true |
| `data-collections` | boolean | true |
| `data-popular-searches` | boolean | true |
| `data-search-button` | boolean | true |
| `data-products` | 4–12 | 8 |

**Theme-rendered HTML passed as `<template>`s** (no extra request, since the theme already has collection context):
- `template[data-nosto-shortcut-filters]` — shortcut filter buttons
- `template[data-nosto-editorial-tile]` with `data-position` — editorial tiles placed by grid slot

Every value falls back, so Nosto still works if the theme doesn't emit an attribute. Grid columns deliberately stay out of this: the theme sets its own `--COLUMNS` variables on the mounts.

Two things to decide, because BaubleBar's set doesn't cover them and ET has both:
1. **Card image mode.** ET's Model | Product switcher needs to know the default mode; our mount currently carries `data-card-image-mode`. BaubleBar has no equivalent.
2. **Sort / filters toggles.** ET's search section has `enable_sort` and `enable_filters` settings; our mount carries those too. BaubleBar always shows both.

My read: adopt BaubleBar's schema exactly as the base, then keep those two as ET-only additions rather than dropping ET theme settings that already exist. But say the word if you'd rather match BaubleBar strictly and drop them.

Both research agents are still running — the full structure map and the theme-side changes. I'll lay out the migration plan when they're back.

The theme-side research is back. Here's BaubleBar's full settings group, which answers your "same settings as BB" directly — it's a dedicated **"RS: Nosto Settings"** group in `config/settings_schema.json`:

**Master switch**
- `rs_nosto_search_enabled` — checkbox, default off

**Header search**
- `rs_nosto_ac_suggestions`, `rs_nosto_ac_collections`, `rs_nosto_ac_popular_searches`, `rs_nosto_ac_search_button` — checkboxes, all default on
- `rs_nosto_ac_products` — range 4–12, default 8
- `rs_nosto_ac_columns_desktop` (2–6, default 4), `rs_nosto_ac_columns_mobile` (1–3, default 2)

**Search page**
- `rs_nosto_search_pagination` — numbers / load-more / infinite, default numbers
- `rs_nosto_search_columns_desktop` (2–6, default 4), `rs_nosto_search_columns_mobile` (1–3, default 2)

**Collection page**
- `rs_nosto_collection_enabled` — checkbox, default off (**separate switch** from search)
- `rs_nosto_collection_pagination` — same three options, default numbers
- `rs_nosto_collection_columns_desktop`, `rs_nosto_collection_columns_mobile`
- `rs_nosto_collection_products_per_page` — range 12–48 step 4, default 24

So our single checkbox buried in the existing search group gets replaced by this group. Columns are passed as `--COLUMNS*` CSS variables on the mount, not read by Nosto at all.

**Four things need your call before I start, because ET genuinely differs:**

1. **The mount can't be a bare div for us.** BaubleBar's `rs-nosto-results.liquid` renders an empty `<div data-nosto-collection>`. ET's `card-scroller-window.js` (the iOS memory fix) and the model switcher both look for `[data-products-grid]` *at page load*. Our `search.liquid` already solves this by nesting the mount inside that wrapper — the collection mount has to do the same. Same settings, different wrapper.

2. **`pushState` vs `replaceState`.** Nosto's `src/lib/url.ts` calls `pushState` on every filter, sort and page change. Your vault rule forbids exactly that — it's the thing that made one Back press drop every loaded page. Fixing it means diverging from the BaubleBar template in `url.ts`.

3. **Infinite scroll + per-card fetch is the 429 risk again, amplified.** At 48 products per page with infinite scroll, deep-linking refetches *all* loaded pages at once, each card firing its own section request. I'd default collection pagination to `numbers` or `load-more` rather than `infinite` until we've measured it on a real ET collection.

4. **BaubleBar's theme side is unmerged.** PR #149 has been open since Oct 8 and the collection work has never shipped. We'd be porting unproven code — worth knowing, not necessarily a blocker.

Also worth noting: ET has no shortcut filters and no editorial metaobject, so those skip cleanly. Our editorial tiles come from section blocks instead, which maps onto Nosto's `data-position` model without changes.

The structure agent is still running. I'll have the full migration plan once it's back.

Both reports are in. Here's the picture and my plan.

## What changed on BaubleBar's side

The restructure is a genuine improvement and worth adopting wholesale:
- `src/` reorganised into `lib/` (no UI) · `elements/` (theme building blocks) · `shared/` (2+ features) · `features/` (one feature)
- CSS Modules gone — one `src/styles.css` with `ns-` prefixes
- Starter leftovers (native mode, Preact card, Storybook) moved to `.unused/` as reference
- `lib/themeSettings.ts` is now the single DOM reader for theme options
- A real **filter drawer** built on Broadcast's slide-out markup — this directly replaces the starter sidebar I flagged as unfinished
- Pagination as a theme setting: numbers / load-more / infinite
- Category/PLP page, shortcut filters, editorial tiles

## Strategy

Take BaubleBar's tree as the new base and re-apply our ET work onto it, rather than merging. The renames are too extensive to merge cleanly, and our ET changes are only two days old and well-scoped. **Nothing we built is wasted** — it all relocates:

|---|---|---|

content.text:
Good stopping point — the Nosto-side migration is done and committed locally. Here's where it landed.

## Done

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `9384953` | BaubleBar's structure adopted unmodified, so our ET diff stays readable |
| `5ea0d4c` | ET identity on package/dev page |
| `1eb019c` | `mountSettings` merged into `themeSettings` — card image mode, sort/filter toggles, switcher + i18n selectors, autocomplete defaults matching the theme dropdown |
| `9a8f458` | ET copy, icons, toolbar |
| `20ba5f9` | ET product card and autocomplete dropdown |
| `ec99ebb` | `replaceState`, per your vault rule |

Everything passes: typecheck, lint, 197 tests, build. The two lint warnings are pre-existing starter ones.

**What we gained from BaubleBar:** the filter drawer built on Broadcast's slide-out markup (replacing the starter sidebar I'd flagged as unfinished), pagination as a theme setting, the editorial-tile placement maths, `themeSettings` as a single settings reader, and a cleaner file layout.

**Where ET won, per your rule:**
- All copy now flows through `lib/i18n.ts` from the theme — BaubleBar hardcodes English in ~15 files and we have 6 locales. ET's wording too: their "Show more" is ET's **"More options"**.
- ET's icons (filled triangles), and no filter icon in the toolbar since the theme doesn't show one.
- Card types are `grid` and `mini` — the dropdown uses `search-product-item`, not the full grid card.
- The dropdown's single "Suggestions" group, and no Popular Searches.
- The toolbar honours the section's `enable_sort` / `enable_filters`, and renders the Model | Product switcher.
- `replaceState`.

## Two things to flag

**1. I left your agent skills alone.** The classifier blocked swapping `.claude`/`.agents`, and I agree with it — installing a different set of instructions for myself is your call. BaubleBar has a useful `nosto-theme-integration` skill plus updated preact/testing/typescript ones; ours are the starter's, and still reference Storybook, which is now in `.unused/`. Want me to port them for your review?

**2. Nothing is verified in a browser.** The Nosto account still isn't provisioned, so this is all code-correct and test-passing but unproven. The filter drawer especially — it reverse-engineers Broadcast's collapsible animation, and I haven't checked it against ET's actual `theme.css`.

## Next
The theme side: the "RS: Nosto Settings" group, a shared `rs-nosto-results.liquid` mount (nested inside `[data-products-grid]`, as ET needs), and the PLP strings added to `nosto-i18n.liquid`. Want me to carry on, or pause here?
